business_rules.statement: Nothing in a module may loosen a pattern; a module may only tighten it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Shared Fallback Pattern Register usage rule
business_rules.applies_to: every module referencing an FB-* pattern

business_rules.statement: Every pattern's terminal safe state is a controlled hold or safe stop. Never promise uninterrupted operation when continuation is unsafe.
Every pattern's recovery ends in reconciliation, and reconciliation always produces an audit record whether or not anything was found.
Stale data is never presented as current. No write control is enabled on a degraded read. Tenant isolation holds absolutely.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen. A partial write is never visible. A write is never queued client-side. Where tenant state cannot be determined, the stricter interpretation applies.

No surface renders the command as applied before acknowledgement. Server-side enforcement state is authoritative regardless of delivery. A stale queued command is never executed. A notification is never the enforcement.
Sending is not delivery; delivery is not opening; opening is not acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not the business action. A notification never enforces anything on its own.
business_rules.enforcement_point: FB-DOH-NOTIF-004 invariants and MOD-DOH-10 honesty rule

business_rules.statement: An action that cannot be audited does not happen. There is no bypass, no buffer, no eventual-audit mode, for any role including the Tenant Admin.
All roles equally; the Root Super Admin has no bypass either.
A partial Summary is never presented as complete. A previous computed output is preserved. Nothing is fabricated to fill a gap.
An import is all-or-nothing per file at V1 so a half-imported worker list cannot exist. No row is silently skipped. No row is silently transformed.
Where state cannot be determined, the stricter interpretation applies. The platform never assumes good standing. Compliance state, once entered, is never relaxed by a failed read.
A truncated export is never delivered as complete. Every export carries its data-as-of timestamp. A PDF Summary carries page numbers, version and an audit hash in its footer.

A misfired occurrence is backfilled, run late against its original due time rather than skipped. Backfill never double-fires: each occurrence carries an idempotency key. A run never finishes earlier than its window because of a scheduler catch-up.
Every functionality in every module section names exactly one governing FB-* pattern.
Every pattern's terminal safe state is a controlled hold or safe stop, never an unbounded retry.
Assert that no fallback path in any pattern permits a cross-tenant read, a qualification bypass, a specification-gate bypass, an approval bypass or a Severity 1 release outside the Quality Manager.
There is no payment integration, no invoicing and no pricing engine at any tier.
No Delivery Operations Hub capability is tier-locked at V1. Custom Job Types, Service Type tags, single sign-on and retention are available uniformly across all tiers.
A tier upgrade is effective immediately and never resets consumed allocation.
Soft suspension blocks exactly the enumerated master-data write classes and leaves exactly the enumerated operational classes open, including recertification of existing workers.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately and delivers the fixed worker-facing message to devices at next contact, never before.
Anonymisation is irreversible; switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later does not, and cannot, restore already-anonymised identities.
The Site level is mandatory — it is the anchor for timezone and shifts. The hierarchy is a platform-wide data-model contract that no surface may fork.
Re-parenting a Location (Cell) or changing hierarchy levels is blocked while in-flight Jobs exist — the sanctioned path is archive-and-recreate.
Archival cascades deliberately: archiving a Site or Area auto-pauses every Job bound to it. The cascade cannot silently strand a standing Job.
Equipment is not a first-class entity at V1; it is referenced through Data Capture only.
Editing a shift never retroactively re-stamps completed runs.
Supervisor permission alone authorises worker-record changes — the audit trail, not a second approval, is the control. Self-attestation of qualifications is not permitted.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform — the specification gates and the evaluation gate are hard and non-configurable.
Notify-only is the platform floor for this gate — no silent posture exists, and no tenant setting can weaken the gate below it.
Qualification expiry raises a four-stage alert at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days. Tenants may add earlier warnings; they may never remove or delay a stage.

At the moment of expiry, under the strict posture, re-assignment to runs requiring the expired certification is blocked. The worker may complete the entire current run. There is no grace period beyond it.
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, regardless of worker, routes to the Quality Manager; the escalation scope is deliberately Area-level, not per-worker.
A clearance lapses automatically at the end of the tenant-set duration and never converts into a qualification; a lapse returns the worker to Expired rather than Valid.
Recertification: the new expiry must be after the previous expiry. Back-dating the issue date is allowed; the platform records both the certification date and the entry date.
Departure is a two-step flow: first reassign all active and upcoming runs, then archive the worker. Open step executions are closed as abandoned with the reason 'Worker departed.'
Re-employment reactivates the prior record — history intact — with a re-validation prompt asking which prior qualifications still apply; nothing is silently re-trusted.
A Job does not embed a workflow — it references one, and where runs exist, each run carries its own workflow.
Segregation of duties is absolute: the user who creates a Job cannot approve that same Job. If the creator also holds the approver role, the platform routes approval to a second qualified approver.
business_rules.enforcement_point: FUNC-DOH-05-2.1.1, enforced at submission and again at approval

business_rules.statement: A tenant must hold an approver role whenever a Job exists; enforced at role removal.
Job Owner is a field on the Job, not a role. It confers no permissions; the five-role model is unchanged by it. It defaults to the creator and is reassignable.
Patch versions apply directly — no Job-Owner decision. Notified-class changes, meaning minor and major, are never silent.
Lane B approved learning changes to package-borne values: never auto-approved, automatically published.
Every run pins its work package at assignment; an in-progress run always completes on the version it started on. Completed runs are immutable.

Modifying the recurrence of an active Job passes the same Quality-Manager approval gate as the Job itself; already-scheduled runs that no longer fit are flagged for an explicit keep-or-cancel decision rather than being silently dropped.
Runs are optional at the tenant's choice of working style — but everything executes as a run; the platform auto-creates a single implicit run where a Job runs without explicit runs.

A run left unstarted after its scheduled start raises a supervisor alert at plus 15 minutes and is auto-cancelled at plus 30 minutes. A partially completed run is treated as cancelled, never complete.
Exactly two in-flight modifications are permitted at V1: worker substitution and end-time extension. All other in-flight structural edits are out of V1.
The word for the final state is `finished` — records close; nothing on the platform is 'sealed'.
The finish (complete to finished) is the one automatic transition on the platform — a data-integrity rule, not a status change; no role can force an early finish.
A Data Capture arriving after run completion is accepted up to the finish window with a `late_arrival` flag and rejected after it. Data from a worker archived in the interim is dual-flagged.

All assignment is supervisor-driven at V1; worker self-assignment is deferred. Assignment always lands on runs, explicit or implicit. There is no availability or double-booking check beyond the qualification check at V1.
Cell narrowing uses the cell-level required-certification model: any holder of that certification may be assigned — there is no per-worker-per-cell grant table to maintain.

Concurrency is unlimited: any number of workers on one run, each on their own identity, with step attribution by individual. Pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker permanently.
Qualification validation runs at three points — assignment, run start and override-carrying screens — so a single bypass at any one point does not open the gate.
The Execution Summary is a computed view, not a stored document; it recomputes as late data lands and every recompute is logged.
Quality Manager review is a tenant-wide toggle, default off, forced on in Regulated-Industry mode; a per-Area toggle is deferred beyond V1. The platform enforces no review service-level agreement.
Any Severity 1 runtime event on the run automatically creates a Critical anomaly in the register, with its containment record attached, regardless of whether review is enabled.
Resolution requires a brief closure note — what was done, and who did it; a resolution without one is refused.

Corrections after finish are append-only annotation records: the original stays immutable, with full who, when and what-changed. There is no re-finalisation in the old sense — the audited recompute with preserved history is the only path.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class or tag; supervisors request release with a note.
There are five fixed roles at V1; custom roles are deferred beyond V1. There is no 'Quality Director' role, and Job Owner is a field, not a role.
Multi-role users are allowed with additive permissions; the audit log records the user identity and the action — never an 'acting as role' fiction.
Two mandatory-role rules are enforced: at least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver role must exist whenever a Job exists. Delegation is deferred beyond V1.
The permission system fails closed: an unresolvable permission denies the request.
Notification channels are in-app and email only — platform-wide, at every tier. In-app notifications cannot be muted.

Three event families always fire and cannot be disabled: subscription and tier lifecycle events; qualification expiry on the 14, 7, 1 and 0-day schedule; and the allocation ladder at 80, 100 and 125 percent plus burst entry.
Users mute sections, not services — the digest service itself cannot be muted.
Nothing is machine-translated at runtime; all content is delivered from English and Spanish locale files.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension or a device command.
The audit log is immutable and append-only. Audit entries commit in the same transaction as the action they record: an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: FUNC-DOH-11-1.1.1, one of six enforced platform invariants with no off position

business_rules.statement: No edit or delete path exists for any audit entry, for any role including the Root Super Admin.
Nothing is purged. Past the hot-retrievability horizon data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable. Retention is uniform across tiers — never tier-gated.
Deletion happens only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the list of applicable standards is owed by the client.
Personal-data anonymisation is the one irreversible act: worker personal data anonymises at 24 months for standard commercial tenants and never in Regulated-Industry mode.
Single sign-on is not tier-gated: SAML and OpenID Connect are both supported on all tiers. Outbound webhooks and directory provisioning are deferred beyond V1.
Enterprise-resource-planning and manufacturing-execution-system integration is out of V1; the inbound endpoint is stubbed and returns HTTP status 501, creating nothing.

All three platform-side access classes appear in Platform Access History, mirrored into the tenant's own audit trail identically: support sessions, the compliance-emergency procedure, and the granted delivery-partner access class.
The tenant can terminate a support session from the banner at any time; every action in the session is logged to the tenant's audit trail. Support access is read-only at V1.

The Hub shows the tenant its own position, read-only — nothing more. No tier configuration, feature gate, pilot management, tenant-group management, impersonation control or usage administration is reachable from the Hub.
The Qualification Calendar has no write capability of any kind; Calendar unavailability affects no enforcement anywhere on the platform.
Cloning resets the name, the state to `draft` — full re-approval required, including segregation of duties — and the recurrence to one-off.
No partial clone can exist; the clone is one transaction.
Cancelling or materially changing one paired Job flags the paired Job's Owner for review — flagging only; no automated behaviour propagates across the link at V1.
A viewer without scope over a paired partner sees only a placeholder, never its content, so pairing cannot become a scope-leak path.

decisions.question: How is remote wipe handled for a device that never returns while holding an unenforced instruction?
decisions.status: open — records the unresolved case for remote wipe
decisions.impact: Bounds the residual risk of a device holding an unenforced instruction.

decisions.question: Is soft suspension released by an explicit operator signal, or automatically on a payment event?
options: (a) operator signal only, no payment integration
(b) payment-event-driven, requiring an integration that §4.2.1 says does not exist
(c) operator signal at V1 with a payment-event path scoped for V2
decisions.adopted_working_position: The operator-signal reading: soft suspension is released by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, taken by the client's platform team when it clears the commercial hold, and the platform observes no payment event because there is no payment integration at V1. The payment-event path is left open and unbuilt.
decisions.status: adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14; client ratification remains outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines whether the platform requires an inbound commercial integration at V1.

decisions.question: Confirmation of 24-month anonymisation under the no-purge model.
decisions.status: open drafting item, presumed yes; Client Decision Required, preserved unresolved
decisions.impact: Determines whether worker identities sever at 24 months for standard commercial tenants.

decisions.question: Is the Site level a required minimum in the location hierarchy?
options: (a) Site mandatory, as §4.3.1 states — every tenant configures at least one Site
(b) Site optional, with timezone and Shift anchored on the tenant record for single-facility tenants
(c) Site mandatory but auto-created as a single default Site at tenant provisioning so the requirement is invisible to simple tenants
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option (c), adopted 2026-08-14 on the instruction of the party commissioning this blueprint. The Site level is mandatory, and the platform auto-creates one default Site at tenant provisioning. That Site is a real Site record with a real identifier, renameable by the Tenant Admin, not a hidden construct.
decisions.status: adopted working position; Derived Clarification — adopted working position, never SoW Fact; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Site is the timezone and shift anchor; without it shifts, cross-midnight production dating and the Worker-Shift meter lose their anchor.

decisions.question: What is the platform-wide default when nobody holding the target escalation role is on shift?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Escalation falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery so the gap is visible rather than silent.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — carried as an open drafting item in §3.9 and Part XII; both the recommended default and its unconfirmed status are preserved
decisions.impact: Determines who receives escalations when the roster has a gap.

decisions.question: Does a Job bind to exactly one Area (hard constraint) or to one parent node at the tenant's configured depth?
options: (a) one Area per Job as a hard constraint, per §4.5.1, with Location used only for cell narrowing at assignment
(b) one parent node per Job at the configured depth, per §2.1, so a three-level tenant binds Jobs to Locations
(c) one parent node per Job with an Area always derivable from it, making the Area binding a computed field rather than a stored constraint
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option (b), adopted 2026-08-14 on the instruction of the party commissioning this blueprint. Part II governs. A Job anchors at the deepest parent node its tenant configured. The §4.5.1 wording 'one Area per Job is a hard constraint' is superseded within this blueprint by 'one parent node per Job'. Every Area-keyed rule resolves from the Job's parent node by walking up to its Area.
decisions.status: adopted working position; Derived Clarification — adopted working position, never SoW Fact; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines Job binding target, drill-down granularity, and whether cell certification narrows through Job or run.

decisions.question: What are the canonical names and codes of the eight starter Job Types and eight starter Service Type tags?
decisions.adopted_working_position: The platform-seeded catalogue of Job Types and Service Type tags ships empty: zero seeded entries at version 1. Every tenant creates its own Job Types and Service Type tags immediately, on every tier, with no platform approval step. When the client supplies the sixteen names and codes they are loaded through the seeded-catalogue publication path and inherited read-only by every tenant workspace.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required for the names and codes; shipping behaviour settled as Derived Clarification — adopted working position, 2026-08-14
decisions.impact: Counts of eight and eight remain source-confirmed; only the names and codes are owed by the client.

decisions.question: How is the contradiction between the Studio's three-stage approval chain and Lane B auto-publication resolved?
decisions.impact: Governs whether approved Lane B learning changes bypass Studio approval staging.

decisions.question: Field-level definition of the Job's unit-model binding, gated on the owed unit-model engineering paper.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required, source gap preserved on the record
decisions.impact: Blocks field-level definition of the Job's parent-node binding and unit mode.

decisions.question: Are the record-finish window's floor of 24 hours and ceiling of 7 days settled values or drafting suggestions?
options: (a) treat 24 hours and 7 days as settled per §4.6.8 and §8.19 and enforce them as rejections
(b) treat them as drafting suggestions per §2.4 and enforce a wider provisional range until confirmed
(c) enforce 24 hours to 7 days at V1 and record the bounds as a floor-register value changeable only through the critical-class change path in the Super Admin platform console
decisions.status: Client Decision Required, preserved unresolved; recommendation is option (c); this chapter builds to 24 hours and 7 days and records the divergence
decisions.impact: The bounds are validated on a tenant setting, so a rejection boundary must be contractual rather than a suggestion.

decisions.question: What do the authority-matrix forms `Supervisor+` and `QM+` mean across five additive, non-hierarchical roles?
options: (a) read the plus forms as role-set membership, so `QM+` means 'holds the Quality Manager role'
(b) define an explicit ordering, which contradicts the stated non-hierarchical model
(c) enumerate every matrix cell by role with no plus form, which is what this chapter does
decisions.status: Client Decision Required, preserved unresolved; recommendation is option (c) for the specification and option (a) as the reading of the source's own matrices
decisions.impact: Every permission cell written as `Supervisor+` is ambiguous between two readings.

decisions.question: Do 'Plant Manager' and 'Quality Director' exist as roles, given §3.5 fixes five roles and denies a Quality Director?
decisions.adopted_working_position: This chapter treats both as personas layered on the five fixed roles and preserves both readings.
decisions.impact: Determines whether Command Center user groups map to roles or to personas.

decisions.question: What is the retrieval expectation for archived data — minutes, hours or next day?
decisions.status: open drafting item; Client Decision Required, preserved unresolved
decisions.impact: Sets the service expectation for tiered, past-horizon data retrieval.

decisions.question: Which named compliance standards require deletion? The list of applicable standards is owed by the client.
decisions.impact: Deletion happens only where a named compliance standard requires it.

contradictions.description: Soft-suspension release: §4.2.4 says the platform acts on an operator signal, not a payment event, and §4.2.1/§8.12 say there is no payment integration; §8.9.2 gives soft exit as 'Automatic on payment' and Part IX says 'soft clears on payment'.
conflicting_values: operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, no payment event observed
Automatic on payment / soft clears on payment

contradictions.description: Minimum hierarchy level: §2.1 marks Site-as-required-minimum as an open drafting item recorded as recommended; §4.3.1 states plainly that 'The Site level is mandatory'. Part XII carries it as an open drafting value.
conflicting_values: Site-as-required-minimum is an open drafting item, recommended not settled (§2.1, Part XII)

contradictions.description: Job parent-node binding: §4.5.1 states 'its single Area binding — one Area per Job is a hard constraint'; §2.1 states the constraint becomes 'one parent node per Job' at the tenant's configured depth.
conflicting_values: one Area per Job is a hard constraint (§4.5.1)
one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth (§2.1)

contradictions.description: Record-finish window bounds: §4.6.8 and §8.19 state the bounds as settled at a floor of 24 hours and a ceiling of 7 days; §2.4 marks the bounds as an open drafting item, suggesting rather than fixing them.
conflicting_values: open drafting item, suggested 24 hours to 7 days (§2.4)

contradictions.description: Studio's three-stage approval chain versus Lane B auto-publication of approved learning changes to package-borne values.
conflicting_values: three-stage approval chain in the Standards and Operations Studio
Lane B auto-publication: never auto-approved, automatically published

contradictions.description: Authority matrices use `Supervisor+` and `QM+` without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles, while the source states multi-role is additive and audit records identity rather than an acting-as-role fiction.
conflicting_values: the named role and any role above it in an undefined hierarchy
any identity holding at least the named role (role-set membership)

contradictions.description: §3.5 states there is no Quality Director and fixes five roles, while §6.1.3 lists 'Plant Manager / Quality Director' as a Client Command Center user group with landing views and escalation-fallback duties, and §5.18 lists 'Plant Manager' in a table headed Fixed role.
conflicting_values: five fixed roles, no Quality Director (§3.5)
Plant Manager / Quality Director as a user group and fixed role (§6.1.3, §5.18)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Circuit breaker opens, or three consecutive read failures, or replica lag beyond tolerance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve from the read replica with an explicit freshness marker and a data-as-of timestamp
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Serve the last successfully loaded view from the browser session with the freshness marker in a warning style and all write controls disabled; then navigate to the Hub home outage notice, which offers no state-changing control
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Full-screen service-unavailable page naming the tenant, the last successful contact time and the support route
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on probe success; the session refetches rather than reusing cached content; degradation recorded as an operational event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: First transaction failure on a master-data or configuration write
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: One bounded, idempotent retry of the whole transaction with a client-generated idempotency key
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Disable the write control, retain the user's typed input, display 'Saving is unavailable — nothing has been lost'; where the tenant-state service is failing, treat the tenant as being in its most recently known suspension state or stricter
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The record is unchanged, the user is told plainly, and no audit entry claims a change occurred
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on probe success; the user re-submits explicitly; reconciliation sweeps for orphaned idempotency keys

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Expected delivery window exceeded for a device command
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continue queuing with ordered delivery preserved, rendering the honest state — issued, propagating, in force per device
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Authorized human escalation to the on-shift Supervisor and Quality Manager with the Quality Manager fallback, marked as a fallback delivery; then a controlled hold blocking new assignment to the affected worker or device
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device continues under its last validly applied state until its offline credential-trust window expires (default ~24 hours, ceiling 72 hours); for a Severity 1 hold the device-local freeze is already in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery at the device's next sync in queued order; replay the ordered queue; every expired-undelivered command recorded as an operational exception, never as applied

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Provider rejection or absent delivery receipt
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery alone, which cannot be muted and therefore always has a landing place
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fall back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback delivery; then inclusion in the next per-shift digest section
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The notification remains in the in-app tray as unread and unacknowledged, visible and ageing, rather than being dropped; Critical unacknowledged after 4 hours re-notifies (1 hour in Regulated-Industry mode)
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic retry with backoff, bounded; then the digest path; reconciliation compares business events against notifications created

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: One bounded idempotent retry of the combined transaction
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refuse the action with a message naming audit unavailability — deliberately no alternate dependency, because an audit written elsewhere is not the audit log; then place the affected write class into a controlled hold
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Writes refused; reads continue; the floor is unaffected because on-device execution and the deterministic layer have no dependency on the tenant audit store
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on one successful audit probe write; reconciliation asserts no business record exists without its audit entry across the outage window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Two consecutive computation failures for one run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Present the last successfully computed output with an explicit 'computation pending' state and its data-as-of timestamp; then present the raw capture list with a statement that the Summary could not compute
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Summary is marked uncomputed; Quality Manager review for that run cannot be completed and the run is held visibly in the review queue rather than passing through unreviewed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recomputation on service restoration; reconciliation compares against the preserved prior output and applies the audited-recompute rule where figures differ materially after finish

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Any validation failure in the file
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reject the file with a per-row, per-column error report the user can download, and write nothing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual single-record entry through the module's own screens; then onboarding assistance from the client's onboarding operation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No records created; the tenant's existing data is untouched; the failed attempt is recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrected re-upload; reconciliation asserts the record-count delta equals the accepted row count exactly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant-state read failure or cache age beyond tolerance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve from the last known state with its age, provided the age is inside tolerance
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Apply the stricter of the last known state and the platform default — for an unreadable state, treating master-data writes as blocked (the soft-suspension class); then read-only for the tenant (the hard-suspension class) with the completion pipeline preserved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Read-only with the completion pipeline open. The floor completes what it started and starts nothing new
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on a fresh state read, lifting the applied restriction in the same act; reconciliation replays tenant_state_history and asserts the applied class matched the true state for every minute

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry with a narrower date or entity filter, suggested to the user with the specific narrower range
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Asynchronous export with in-app notification when ready; then render the data on screen with pagination
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No file produced, and the user is told plainly that no file was produced. A partial file is never offered
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-run; reconciliation compares exported row counts against the source query count and reports any mismatch rather than shipping the file

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An expected scheduled occurrence not executed within its tolerance (a misfire)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Immediate backfill of the missed occurrence with its original due time preserved on the record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual trigger by platform operations, audited as a manual intervention; for the run auto-close scheduler specifically the run remains `complete` and stays open to late data rather than finishing — extending a window is safe, shortening it is not
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Records remain in their current state, visibly overdue, rather than being advanced on incomplete information
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Backfill, then resume the normal schedule; reconciliation compares expected against executed occurrences and asserts every gap is backfilled with duplicate-fire count zero
